It is often given as a name to infants in the hope that they will grow up to be individuals who bring joy, prosperity, and auspiciousness into their families and society. The name is deeply ingrained in the values of Indian culture, where happiness, good fortune, and positivity are cherished and sought after.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name "Subas" resonates with the concept of inner joy and happiness. It reflects the idea of living a life filled with contentment and good fortune, which is a significant goal in Hindu spiritual practices. The name is believed to bring blessings of the gods and spiritual prosperity, which can help individuals on their spiritual journey towards self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Subas is derived from the Sanskrit word "Subh," meaning good, auspicious, or blessed. This name is a reminder to always strive for good and seek the blessings of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Subas Chandra Bose was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who advocated for India's independence from British rule through violent means. He formed the Indian National Army (INA) in 1942, with the help of the Japanese, to wage war against the British in South East Asia. Subas is also known for his call for 'Quit India' during a speech at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai on 8 August 1942.

historical_references.reference: Subas Patrakar is an ancient Hindu sage and astronomer known for his contributions to the field of Indian astronomy. He lived during the 6th century CE and is believed to have compiled the Siddhantasiromani, a comprehensive astronomical work containing various astronomical theories and calculations. Subas Patrakar is also known for his astronomical work, the Surya Siddhanta, which is considered one of the most authoritative astronomical texts in ancient India.
